review.summary: Static adversarial review of the composition source at public head 895a6212c2f5bb5942189707e855683bf975438d: main768f843, plus the five selected Codex code paths, three selected design/evidence documents, and the README, master adapter and verification text. Severity count: no Critical, High or Medium; five Low. Findings 1 and 2 re-assess the two existing pending limits. Finding 3 is a documentation precision issue. Findings 4 and 5 are test-control robustness issues. (1) No-custody behaviour matches main. custody_pool() returns None outside cfg(test). With Control.custody set to None, finish_no_work, holds_resources, the RegisteredTransition::drop early return, the extra register_existing refusal and the stop() CustodyHeld branch all reduce to main behaviour. The no-custody Control::spawn branch is equivalent to main's. The job_revoked flag set by stop() and CallerGuard is read only by custody handlers, so it has no effect elsewhere. Preparation first-cause and consumption, Lost publication, exact Arc restoration and the strict original_disposition gate (CREATED, all joined, no Unknown or outstanding work, no published Lost) are not weakened. (2) No lock reentry found. Lock order is registry, then leaf locks (custody, phase, published). The endpoint lock is taken before inventory.open. No lock is held across runtime.spawn, Begin send or synchronous future drop. Creator and worker joins, and drops of retired Entry, Control or intent values, happen outside the pool and registry locks. (3) Failure paths are handled conservatively. On closed runtime, missing runtime, caller Drop, and actor, callback or worker panic, job slots stay charged unless genuinely joined or observed NotCreated. Created outstanding work is never removed from the registry. The reply-after-retirement ordering is correct for the current handlers. (4) No public API is added. CodexAdapter capabilities remain empty, probe and release refuse, transport_succeeded is false, and the custody module is private. (5) Regression attribution: I found no source-level causal path from the selected changes to the seven failed Grok consumers. The diff touches only codex/* and docs, the process-wide Pool is never reserved, and custody shares no mutable state with Grok. Test-time load from the new controls cannot be excluded: sleep-polling custodian threads at 1 ms (up to 21 at once in the capacity control), fixture worker threads, a deliberate 2 s wait, and git-spawning Fixture and ApprovalFixture setup. The base README also records unexplained full-run failures. Cause and contribution therefore remain UNKNOWN and are not attributed either way. (6) Approval scope: the composed selected mechanical source only.

findings.causal_reproduction: Two predicates make the same hold decision at different times. finish_no_work (attempt.rs ~227) holds when outstanding_effects is true, or when created is true and either outstanding or unknown is true. holds_resources (~202) is evaluated later by RegisteredTransition::drop (session.rs ~203). For an exact Fresh or Restored phase it exempts only !created && !unknown && !outstanding_effects; otherwise it holds on outstanding, or on created && unknown. Two state classes make finish_no_work choose plain no-work while holds_resources then holds. In that case drop returns early without a DelayedDisposition, the transition flag stays claimed, reconcile_custody (which acts only on intents) never visits the entry, and register_existing refuses the non-terminal Starting snapshot. The result is a permanent entry counting toward RETAINED_TERMINALS. Class A: create_worker's std spawn returns Err (custody.rs ~651), giving created=false, unknown=true, effects=0; the Create request is retired before its reply; any Note is still accepted at drop time. Class B: the created worker has already joined (effects=0) when finish_no_work runs, and a Note is accepted before drop. In the current inventory the only non-test Note producer is Control::finished, which notes only when created && outstanding, which is false in both classes; take_endpoint is cfg(test). Class A also needs a real OS thread-creation failure in the cfg(test) Create path, and no control injects one. Without a queued Note, class A behaves conservatively: the entry is removed and the attempted-worker slot stays charged. The failure direction is fail-closed (registry availability loss, not custody loss). Production cannot reach it because custody_pool() is None. Not reproduced. It stays Low under the current inventory. Class B becomes reachable as soon as the Ok/Starting post-return endpoint or any new Note producer is activated.
findings.correction: Decide the hold classification once. Compute it in finish_no_work (or a shared function over one counter snapshot) and record it on Control. RegisteredTransition and register_existing should consume that recorded decision instead of re-reading live counters. Then either record a DelayedDisposition for every held no-work outcome, or exempt metadata-only outstanding work uniformly. Before any factory, handler or endpoint activation, add a cfg(test) create_worker spawn-Err seam, controls for class A with a queued Note and for class B (created and joined, then a racing Note), and record compiled mutants for both.

findings.causal_reproduction: In run(), the Create reply Sender is moved into the catch_unwind closure. A panic inside create_worker before created=true would drop the reply during unwind, before inflight, accepted and effect_requests are retired (~521-526). The actor's response.await would then fail with 'preparation creator lost' while effect_requests==1. finish_no_work would freeze CustodyHeld with created=false. original_disposition requires created, so the entry and its intent would be retained forever. If the panic came before worker_attempted=true, the custodian would later return WorkerDisposition::NotCreated with the actor joined. Pool::drain would then release all three slots (n==3) while unknown=true leaves joined=false and the Entry retained. This is the Unknown-plus-full-refund case recorded as Source1 Low (b). The current handler inventory has no such panic site. Note handling cannot panic. In create_worker the only panic is the injected assert, which runs after the worker, created and effects stores. Lock poisoning uses into_inner, and Builder::spawn returns Err rather than panicking. This is hypothetical. Registry retention would be fail-closed, but the pre-attempt variant would refund unproved slots (fail-open).
findings.correction: Destructure each request before catch_unwind so the reply Sender and the effect-request marker stay in the outer frame. On a caught panic, send an explicit Err only after retirement. Attribute any handler panic to the worker frame (for example, set worker_attempted so the disposition is Unknown, never NotCreated), so Pool::drain cannot refund a frame that has no proof. Add an injected pre-attempt handler-panic control and its mutant before any handler is added.

findings.causal_reproduction: Four documentation statements differ from the supplied code and controls. (1) The master text says an error with a created resource retains the registry entry and deferred original disposition, and that only observed complete joins permit removal or restoration. The supplied worker_join_before_error_preserves_zero_effect_registry_disposition control and the 'Bookkeeping versus resource hold' mutant show otherwise for a worker that joined before the context error: ordinary removal happens immediately while the actor and custodian are still unjoined. (2) After an actor panic or runtime drop following creation, the outcome is Lost. RegisteredTransition::drop then holds the entry with its transition claimed and no deferred disposition, and no reconcile or release path exists; the master text does not say this. (3) The imported component design lists 'terminal eviction' as a consumer, but Codex session.rs has no eviction; RETAINED_TERMINALS only refuses new registrations. (4) The verification doc (~49) says the closed fixture creates no native or Git subprocess. The factory does not, but every custody control's Fixture or ApprovalFixture setup runs git (init/add/commit, WorktreeManager::create, and verify_git through bounded_git). That matters for the load-based regression question. Overall the wording is stricter than the behaviour in one place and silent in others; nothing is made unsafe.
findings.correction: Reword the master section. A context error while a created resource is outstanding or Unknown freezes CustodyHeld and records the deferred disposition. A resource already joined before the error follows ordinary no-work removal or restoration. Lost with created resources is held without a reconcilable disposition and needs future recovery. Remove or qualify 'terminal eviction' in the component design. In the verification doc, state that the custody factory spawns no subprocess while the controls' repository setup does run git.

findings.causal_reproduction: In revoked_create_with_note(false), the 'reply before own effect-request retirement' mutant is caught only if the actor reaches AfterCustodyFactory within a 2 s tokio timeout while retirement is paused. If it does not, the test drops the pause, the late gate release lets the error arm run after retirement, finish_no_work sees no outstanding effect, and the final FreshUnpublished assertion passes, so the mutant survives. The documented macOS load (inspection deadline overshoots above 300 ms, 60 s watchdogs) does not guarantee that window. The correct implementation also always spends the full 2 s. The recorded 16/16 kill is therefore a host-time observation, not a timing-independent guarantee. The shared 2 s wait() helper can likewise fail correct code under load.
findings.correction: Replace the timeout-based detection for the non-Note case with a deterministic cfg(test) hook. For example, set a flag if a reply is sent while that request's retirement is incomplete, assert it is never set, and keep the gate-based overlap only for the note_pending case. Consider scaling or removing fixed 2 s observation deadlines where the correct path waits on a real event.

findings.causal_reproduction: The component design requires omit-precheck and omit-lock-release mutants to alter the custodied closed-runtime consumer. Neither appears in the historical 13+3 tables or in the composition's 16-operator table. The legacy attempt.rs control runs spawn on a helper thread with recv_timeout specifically so a deadlock mutant fails within a bound. Both custodied closed-runtime controls (custodied_missing_and_closed_runtime_have_exact_no_effect_accounting and actual_registration_missing_and_closed_runtime_have_no_native_effects) call Control::spawn or spawn_launch(..).now_or_never() directly on the test thread. A mutant that holds Control.task across runtime.spawn would deadlock in TaskGuard -> release_task during the synchronous drop of the wrapped future, and would hang the test binary instead of failing. The omit-precheck mutant would probably be killed by the unwrap_err and used()==0 assertions, but that kill is not recorded.
findings.correction: Run the custodied closed-runtime spawn on a helper thread with a bounded recv_timeout, as the legacy control does. Add the omit-precheck and omit-lock-release operators to the recorded compiled mutation set for this composition.

review.summary:
Static composition review of public head 895a6212c2f5bb5942189707e855683bf975438d (draft PR69), using only the supplied packet. Five Codex code paths are imported onto main 768f843, and the supplied dependencies preparation.rs, ownership.rs, availability.rs and policy.rs are unchanged.

Production custody selection is structurally None. custody_pool returns None outside cfg(test), and Create, FileSpec, Factory and effect_requests are all cfg(test). Every non-fixture path therefore behaves the same as main:
- refused_before_work and the context-error arms go through finish_no_work, which reduces to finished() when custody is None.
- holds_resources() is false, and CustodyHeld cannot occur without custody.
- The revoke_jobs call added to stop() sets an inert latch.
- reconcile_custody runs only after availability.require(). The public EMPTY refusal still comes before any registry, Store, process or Git work.
- capabilities, probe, release and transport_succeeded are unchanged.

None of these is weakened: Preparation first-cause, the consumed no-interrupt behaviour (CallerGuard revokes jobs and cancel() is a no-op on Consumed), published-Lost handling, and strict original_disposition (created, all three frames pool-joined, not unknown, not outstanding, no published Lost, exact Arc owner).

I found no fail-open path:
- No slot is refunded without an observed join or a creator-reported NotCreated, and worker_attempted is set before the thread spawn.
- No registry entry is removed or restored while a created worker is unjoined, because effects and accepted keep holds_resources true.
- The file effect cannot happen before the installed Begin.
- Create replies only after its counters are retired.
- The open mutex serializes the last accept against the custodian's close.

Lock ordering in the supplied code has no cycle. The registry lock is taken before the custody, endpoint and open locks. The pool lock is never held across a join or drop, Control.task is never held across runtime.spawn, and the endpoint lock is only ever followed by the open lock. The closed-runtime synchronous drop inside runtime.spawn takes no lock that spawn holds.

There are no Critical, High or Medium findings. There are four Lows, listed in findings. Finding 1 is new (abandonment does not set the job-revocation latch). The two pending Lows are re-rated Low for the current inventory (both are fail-closed over-retention or hypothetical). Finding 4 is documentation precision.

Regression: no code path from the selected changes reaches the 7 failing Grok consumers. The only conceivable channel is shared-process load from the 18 added controls. That channel is unmeasured, and cause and component contribution remain UNKNOWN.

APPROVED: the selected composition SOURCE only, as a private, cfg(test)-activated mechanical custody component.

NOT APPROVED:
- Merge or limited-merge readiness. PR69 must stay draft and unmerged.
- Any native, CPP, schema or PR39 readiness.

findings.causal_reproduction:
NEW. Not executed; constructible only with existing cfg(test) seams.

Abandonment publishes Lost without setting the job-revocation latch. TaskGuard::drop (attempt.rs ~402-428) and the RegisteredTransition::drop abandonment branch (session.rs ~177-197) call finished(Lost) but never revoke_jobs().

Sequence:
1. Use the adapter() fixture with a FileSpec and call Inventory::pause(true).
2. Let the actor reach Factory::run, so Inventory::create is accepted (accepted==1, effect_requests==1) and the actor awaits its oneshot.
3. Call control.abort_owned_task(), which uses the TaskOwner::Observed AbortHandle.
4. The actor future drops at that await. RegisteredTransition and TaskGuard publish Finished(Lost). The result Sender drops, so spawn_launch receives SessionLost and disarms CallerGuard on its normal path; no revocation happens.
5. Call Inventory::pause(false). run() handles the still-queued Create with permitted=true, because the custodian's retained Arc keeps the owner alive and job_revoked is false.
6. create_worker spawns the worker, which creates and writes the file after both the requester and the caller have ended.

Containment stays fail-closed. RegisteredTransition saw accepted>0 and retained the entry, and the cancelled actor join makes custody Unknown and keeps one slot. There is no release and no fail-open.

The defect is that a NEW effect is admitted after abandonment, contrary to 'cancellation revokes new effects'. The production-shaped trigger needs runtime shutdown to drop the actor task before the armed caller. Create is cfg(test)-only, so the current production inventory cannot reach this.

PENDING (Source2 reviewer A). Unreproduced; re-rated Low for the current inventory.

Mechanism:
1. create_worker's Builder::spawn Err branch (custody.rs ~646) sets unknown=true with created=false, after worker_attempted=true.
2. The Create retires before its reply, so the actor's context arm runs finish_no_work with outstanding_effects()=false and created=false.
3. finish_no_work therefore publishes a plain FreshUnpublished or RestoredBeforeAdmission, and RegisteredTransition records no DelayedDisposition.
4. If a fixed Note is still accepted when RegisteredTransition drops, holds_resources() skips its no-work exemption (because unknown=true) and returns outstanding()=true.
5. The entry keeps transition=true and is never revisited, because reconcile_custody only acts on entries that have an intent.

Effect: one of the 32 registry slots on that adapter is occupied permanently, plus the pool's Unknown worker slot. The direction is fail-closed over-retention; nothing is removed or refunded early.

Reachability:
- The OS thread-creation failure is genuinely possible inside fixtures.
- The Note leg needs an externally held endpoint. finished() only sends its own note when created=true, and the only other issuer is the cfg(test) take_endpoint.
- Create itself is cfg(test), and production custody selection is None.
findings.correction:
Make finish_no_work and holds_resources evaluate one shared, explicitly chosen predicate for the !created && unknown case. Either:
- select CustodyHeld, so the retention is labelled and observable; or
- treat it as bookkeeping-only like the zero-effect case, since the pool already retains the unproved slot.

Before any factory or handler activation, add a cfg(test) worker-spawn-Err injection seam, a queued-Note control and a mutant.

findings.causal_reproduction:
PENDING (the shared Source2 Low and Source1 Low b). Hypothetical; unreachable with the current handlers.

(i) A future handler that panics before created=true drops the request, including the Create reply Sender, inside catch_unwind before retirement. The actor's create() wakes with 'preparation creator lost' while effect_requests and accepted are still charged. finish_no_work then selects CustodyHeld with created=false, which original_disposition can never reconcile. This is fail-closed.

(ii) If that panic also comes before worker_attempted is set, run() reports WorkerDisposition::NotCreated. drain then computes n=3 and decrements used by 3 even though unknown=true. complete=false keeps the entry, but the counter is refunded. This is fail-open accounting, but only under a hypothetical handler.

Current inventory:
- Note handling has no panic site.
- Create's only panic sites are the injected assert, which runs after created and effects are set, and File::create or the assert inside the worker thread.
- Those yield Unknown or held results, as the panic-before-Begin control shows.
findings.correction:
Before adding any handler or activating the factory:
1. Retire request counters in a guard that runs before the reply Sender can drop, or reply with a typed failure after retirement on the unwind path.
2. Make drain refund only dispositions proven per frame. Treat NotCreated as unproved whenever an unattributed handler panic has set unknown or worker_uncertain.
3. Add seam controls and compiled mutants for both.

findings.causal_reproduction:
Documentation precision only; no runtime effect.

(a) The master sentence 'An error with a created resource retains the exact registry entry and deferred original disposition' is not exact.
- When the created worker has already joined before the context arm, the original no-work removal happens immediately (the worker_join_before_error control).
- An abandoned (Lost) actor with an outstanding resource is retained with no deferred disposition at all and is never reconciled.

(b) The component design (doc/design/issue-19-lifetime-component-design.md ~184 and ~213) names a Codex 'terminal eviction' consumer that does not exist in session.rs. Codex release() refuses, and only the 32-entry admission cap applies. The claim is vacuous rather than unsafe.

(c) doc/verification/issue-19-native-custody.md ~48 says 'the closed fixture creates no native/Git subprocess'. That is true of the resource factory only. The selected controls' setup runs /usr/bin/git (Fixture::new), and the two checkpoint controls also run bounded_git under process-group inspection (the recorded sandbox PermissionDenied). This matters for the shared-process regression question.
findings.correction:
Reword the three statements:
- Retention applies while a created resource is outstanding or Unknown, and Lost or abandoned retention has no deferred disposition.
- Drop or qualify the terminal-eviction consumer.
- State that fixture setup spawns Git and macOS inspection subprocesses, even though the custody resource itself does not.

scope_limits: Method: static review of the supplied public packet only. No tools, execution, file operations or peer findings were used. Line numbers were counted by hand from the packet and may be off by a few lines; the function names in each reproduction are authoritative.

Not reviewed (omitted from the packet): codex/protocol.rs, codex/transport.rs, crate::adapter (ProcessGroup, cleanup_group, inspection), the state Store, the Grok adapter and its tests, and the remaining session.rs tests. Grok failure mechanisms therefore cannot be analysed. The provenance and blob-identity statements are accepted as stated, not independently verified.

NOT APPROVED: merge or limited-merge readiness.
- Full default Debug remains RED at 282 passed, 7 failed, 23 ignored, with unexplained cause.
- Full Release workspace tests were not run.
- Exact final-head macOS and Linux CI is not supplied.
- The 857 and a8aa951 CI failures remain public.
No same-head retry and no deadline, parallelism, latch or budget waiver is accepted. PR69 must stay draft and unmerged while the full gates and the broad native/backend WHAT dependency remain open.

The recorded results are author observations that were not reproduced here: 18 Debug and 18 Release controls, 121 affected Release Codex controls, and 16 compiled assertion kills followed by 18 restored passes. They are not a certificate of native, delegated or descendant settlement, and raw native metrics are not treated as qualified usage.

Source1 Low (a) is a custodian polling forever if the actor is never installed after install_custody. It remains unreachable in current consumers, because Control::spawn cannot fail on a fresh Vacant Control after install_custody. It stays an activation limit.
